Maybe you're running cold outreach for sales or sourcing candidates for a role. Or you're in marketing like me and want to bring up the idea of a partnership with someone whose inbox you can't find. Either way, you have a name and a company, and you need the email address that goes with them. An email finder API turns those two into an address you can use, and the good ones tell you how sure they are. Every vendor uses a different request shape, a different credit model, and a different idea of what counts as a result, so the API you pick shapes your code as much as your hit rate.


This guide compares nine email finder APIs on what a developer needs before writing the integration: the endpoint, the inputs, rate limits, the free tier, and what a call costs. Every price and limit comes from the provider's own pricing page or docs, checked on November 19, 2026. Where a provider is also available in Firecrawl Alexandria, the guide also shows how it performed on live agent calls.


## What is an email finder API?


An email finder API is an endpoint that takes a person's first and last name plus their company's domain or name, and returns the work email address that person most likely uses. Most also return a confidence score or a deliverability status, and many charge only when an address is provided.


Providers combine three sources to get there: addresses they have seen published on the web, the naming pattern a company uses (first.last@, f.last@, and so on), and a live check against the company's mail server. A provider that only guesses the pattern is fast but often wrong. One that checks the mail server takes longer, and each provider has its own rules for catch-all domains, which accept mail for any address.


Finding and verifying are separate jobs. A finder creates an email address from a name you provide, and a verifier tests the email you already have. Most finders in this list run a deliverability check on what they return, so you rarely need a second call.


## How do you choose an email finder API?


Five things decide which email finder API fits your project. Hit rate matters too, but it varies with your list, so test each candidate on 50 to 100 people whose addresses you already know.


1. **Inputs.** Every API here accepts a name plus a domain. Hunter, Anymail Finder, and Icypeas also accept a company name when you don't know the domain, which saves a lookup step.
2. **Billing on a miss.** Most vendors below say a search that finds nothing is free. Read each one's rule for repeat lookups too, since some don't charge twice for the same person within a set period.
3. **Rate limits.** Hunter publishes 15 requests per second on its email finder. Snov.io publishes 60 requests per minute across its API. Anymail Finder says it has no daily caps.
4. **Sync or async.** Hunter and Findymail answer in the same request. Enrow, Icypeas, and Snov.io return a job ID, then deliver the result by polling or webhook.
5. **Where it runs.** If an agent in ChatGPT, Claude, or Cursor does the lookups, an MCP server helps, and Firecrawl Alexandria lets you use several email finders without setting each one up separately.

- **Email finders on one key:**[Hunter](https://alexandria.firecrawl.dev/providers/hunter) ,[Prospeo](https://alexandria.firecrawl.dev/providers/prospeo) ,[Findymail](https://alexandria.firecrawl.dev/providers/findymail) ,[Anymail Finder](https://alexandria.firecrawl.dev/providers/anymailfinder) ,[Icypeas](https://alexandria.firecrawl.dev/providers/icypeas) ,[Enrow](https://alexandria.firecrawl.dev/providers/enrow) , and[Dropcontact](https://alexandria.firecrawl.dev/providers/dropcontact) , plus other finders and verifiers in the[people category](https://alexandria.firecrawl.dev/categories/people) .

## 2. Hunter


Hunter's email finder takes a name and a domain or company name and returns the most likely address with a confidence score from 0 to 100, the public pages where the address was seen, and the result of an automatic deliverability check.


- **Endpoint:**` GET https://api.hunter.io/v2/email-finder` , with` domain` or` company` plus` first_name` and` last_name` or` full_name` . An optional` max_duration` (3 to 20 seconds) lets Hunter spend longer refining a result.
- **Rate limit:** 15 requests per second and 500 requests per minute on the email finder, per Hunter's[API documentation](https://hunter.io/api-documentation/v2#email-finder) .
- **Billing:** the docs state that no credit is charged when no email is found, and the pricing page says each repeated search counts once per calendar month.
- **Other endpoints:** Domain Search lists the addresses Hunter knows at a company, and the Email Verifier checks an address you already have.


**Pricing:** on[Hunter's pricing page](https://hunter.io/pricing) , the free plan included 50 credits a month and the Starter plan cost $49 a month billed monthly for 2,000 credits. Hunter's API page says you don't need a paid plan to use the API.


**Best for:** developers who want detailed documentation, published limits, and a confidence score on every result.[Hunter](https://alexandria.firecrawl.dev/providers/hunter) is also in Firecrawl Alexandria.


## 3. Prospeo


[Prospeo](https://alexandria.firecrawl.dev/providers/prospeo) returns a person's work email through its Enrich Person endpoint, alongside the rest of their B2B profile, and handles up to 50 people at once with Bulk Enrich Person. Its person and company search endpoints help you build a list before you look anyone up.


- **Endpoints:** Enrich Person for one lead and Bulk Enrich Person for up to 50, per[Prospeo's API docs](https://prospeo.io/api-docs) .
- **Billing:** one credit per email found and zero when none is found, per the pricing FAQ. A mobile number costs 10 credits.
- **Rate limits:** set per plan. Prospeo's pricing table lists separate enrich and search API limits for Starter, Growth, and Pro, with the highest limits on Pro.


**Pricing:** on[Prospeo's pricing page](https://prospeo.io/pricing) , the free plan included 100 credits a month and paid plans started at $49 a month billed monthly for 2,000 credits. Credits reset each billing cycle and don't roll over.


**Best for:** fast single lookups. Prospeo had the lowest P95 latency of the providers in this guide on Firecrawl Alexandria's benchmark (414 ms).


## 4. Findymail


Findymail's email finder takes a full name and a company domain in one POST request and returns the contact with their address. For large batches it supports webhook-based async processing, so your application doesn't wait on each lookup.


- **Endpoint:**` POST https://app.findymail.com/api/search/name` with` name` and` domain` , authenticated with a bearer token, per Findymail's email finder API page.
- **Billing:** the API page says you pay only when an email is found, and the pricing page says Findymail doesn't charge again for an address you found in the previous 30 days.
- **Extras:** every plan includes API and MCP access, reverse email lookup, and phone finding.


**Pricing:** on[Findymail's pricing page](https://www.findymail.com/pricing/) , prospecting plans started at $99 a month, with usage measured over rolling 5-hour and 7-day windows rather than credits. Credit-based plans for teams that resell data also started at $99 a month, for 5,000 finder credits at one credit per email.


**Best for:** sales teams that want a flat monthly plan instead of counting credits. You can find[Findymail](https://alexandria.firecrawl.dev/providers/findymail) in Firecrawl Alexandria, too.


## 5. Anymail Finder


Anymail Finder's API finds a person's email from a name and a domain or company name, and adds lookups that start from less: all the addresses it holds at a company, or the address of the person in a given role.


- **Endpoints:** Find Person Email, Find Company Emails, Find Decision Maker Email, Verify Email, and Reverse Email Lookup, per[Anymail Finder's API docs](https://anymailfinder.com/email-finder-api/docs) , which also publish an OpenAPI spec and an MCP server.
- **Rate limit:** the docs say there are no daily API call caps.
- **Billing:** a person search costs 1 credit and is charged only when an email comes back. Company emails cost 1 credit for up to 20 addresses, and a decision maker lookup costs 2 credits.


**Pricing:** on[Anymail Finder's pricing page](https://anymailfinder.com/pricing) , plans started at $29 a month for 400 credits, and every monthly plan came with a 7-day trial and 100 credits.


**Best for:** role-based prospecting, when you know the company and the job title but not the name. You can also call[Anymail Finder](https://alexandria.firecrawl.dev/providers/anymailfinder) through Firecrawl Alexandria.


## 6. Icypeas


Icypeas finds a professional email from a first name, a last name, and a domain or company name. Each search is asynchronous. The first call returns an ID at once, and you read the result a few seconds later by polling or through a webhook while Icypeas checks the address with the mail server.


- **Endpoint:**` POST https://app.icypeas.com/api/email-search` with` firstname` ,` lastname` , and` domainOrCompany` , per the[Icypeas API docs](https://api-doc.icypeas.com/) , which also publish an` llms.txt` file and an OpenAPI spec.
- **Billing:** 1 credit if an email is found, and 0.1 credit per verification.
- **Bulk:** up to 5,000 rows in a single bulk call.


**Pricing:** on[Icypeas's pricing page](https://www.icypeas.com/pricing) , the Basic plan cost $19 a month plus VAT for 1,000 credits, credits rolled over, and a limited-time offer gave new accounts 50 free credits.


**Best for:** large files at a low cost per email.[Icypeas](https://alexandria.firecrawl.dev/providers/icypeas) is one of the email finders in Firecrawl Alexandria as well.


## 7. Enrow


[Enrow](https://alexandria.firecrawl.dev/providers/enrow) 's email finder is asynchronous by design. You POST a search, get an ID back at once, and receive the email and its qualification by webhook or by polling a GET endpoint. The response reports the credits each search used.


- **Endpoint:**` POST https://api.enrow.io/email/find/single` , authenticated with an` x-api-key` header, per[Enrow's API docs](https://docs.enrow.io/) . A verifier endpoint uses the same flow.
- **Billing:** "No result, no charge", per the pricing page. One pool of credits covers the email finder, phone finder, and verifier.


**Pricing:** on[Enrow's pricing page](https://enrow.io/pricing) , plans started at $17 a month for 1,000 credits, and every plan listed 50 free credits and API access.


**Best for:** backends that already handle webhooks and want a low entry price. Enrow had the most calls of any provider in this guide in the benchmark window (37.9K).


## 8. Dropcontact


[Dropcontact](https://alexandria.firecrawl.dev/providers/dropcontact) finds and qualifies B2B work emails and enriches contacts with company data. You reach it through a REST API, a hosted MCP server for AI assistants, or a Google Sheets add-on, all on the same account and credits.


- **Access:** a REST API authenticated with an` X-Access-Token` header, per the[Dropcontact developer docs](https://developer.dropcontact.com/) .
- **Billing:** an email Dropcontact doesn't find is credited back, per the pricing FAQ, and an optional carryover keeps unused credits.


**Pricing:** on[Dropcontact's pricing page](https://www.dropcontact.com/pricing) , plans were priced by monthly credit volume in euros, with 50 free credits to start.


**Best for:** teams that want email finding inside a spreadsheet or an AI assistant as well as in code. Dropcontact is available in Firecrawl Alexandria, too.


## 9. Snov.io


Snov.io's API finds emails from a name and a domain as part of a wider sales platform that also covers prospect search, verification, and email campaigns. Each lookup starts a task and then fetches its result with the task hash.


- **Endpoints:**` POST https://api.snov.io/v2/emails-by-domain-by-name/start` , then` GET https://api.snov.io/v2/emails-by-domain-by-name/result` , per[Snov.io's API docs](https://snov.io/api) .
- **Rate limit:** 60 requests per minute across the API.
- **Billing:** credits are shared across prospect search, email search, and email verification.


**Pricing:** on[Snov.io's pricing page](https://snov.io/pricing) , the free Trial plan renewed every month with 50 credits, and the Starter plan cost $39 a month billed monthly for 1,000 credits.


**Best for:** teams that want the email finder and the outreach tool on one account.


## Why is an email finder API aggregator better than a single provider?


An email finder API aggregator puts several providers behind one API, so the share of your list that gets an address no longer depends on one vendor's database. Firecrawl Alexandria works as that aggregator for email finding, with seven of the providers in this guide on one Firecrawl key, each returning JSON from the same call.


- **More rows filled.** Providers build their data from different sources, so each finds addresses the others miss, and hit rates change from one list to the next. When one provider comes back empty, your agent passes the row to the next one on the same key.
- **One integration to maintain.** The vendors above use different authentication, field names, and delivery models (some answer in the request, others by webhook). Through Firecrawl Alexandria you keep one client, and trying a new provider means changing the provider in the request and mapping its inputs.
- **A fallback when a provider struggles.** In the benchmark above, completion rates ranged from 88.9% to 100% and P95 latency from 414 ms to 93.5 seconds. An agent can route around whichever provider is slow or erroring that day.
- **Lower cost per email found.** The work email waterfall tries providers in cost order and stops at the first confident hit, so the pricier providers only see the rows the cheaper ones missed.

## How do you call several email finder APIs from one agent?


Firecrawl Alexandria lets one agent call several email finder APIs with the same key and request shape, then fall back from one to the next when a lookup comes back empty. Without it, each vendor needs its own account, key, client code, and retry logic, not to mention the time wasted wiring them all together.


In the usual waterfall pattern, you start with the cheapest provider that covers your market, send only the missing contacts to the next one, and record which source answered each row so you can audit the list later. With direct integrations, that means a client per vendor and a mapping layer to make their responses look alike. Through Firecrawl Alexandria every response comes back as JSON from the same` scrape` call, so the fallback is a loop over providers.


The same works without code. Connect Firecrawl to ChatGPT, Claude, Cursor, or Claude Code, then paste a list with a prompt like this:


```text
Use Firecrawl Alexandria to find the work email for each person on this list
(first name, last name, company domain). Try the cheapest email finder first,
only retry the rows it misses with another provider, and tell me which provider
answered each row and what it cost.
```


Again, you can use our work email waterfall tool, which packages that brief so you can copy it into any connected assistant. For enrichment beyond the email, such as firmographics for each company, see our guide to the[best company enrichment APIs](https://www.firecrawl.dev/blog/best-company-enrichment-api) and the[complete guide to data enrichment](https://www.firecrawl.dev/blog/complete-guide-to-data-enrichment) .


## Which email finder API should you pick?


Pick a single vendor when one provider already covers your market and you want its own dashboard and plan. If you'd rather not bet on one provider, start with Firecrawl Alexandria.


- **Firecrawl Alexandria** if you want the best chance of finding every email, because when one provider misses, your agent tries the next one on the same key and the same bill.
- **Hunter** if you want to build against detailed docs, because it publishes its rate limits and returns a confidence score you can set a threshold on.
- **Prospeo** if speed matters, because it had the lowest P95 latency of the providers in this guide on Firecrawl Alexandria's benchmark and enriches up to 50 people per bulk request.
- **Findymail** if you'd rather budget a flat monthly fee, because its prospecting plans measure usage over time windows instead of credits.
- **Anymail Finder** when you know the company and role but not the person, because its Find Decision Maker Email endpoint looks people up by job title.
- **Icypeas** and **Enrow** for large batches on a small budget, because they have the lowest listed entry prices in this guide and return results by webhook, so a big batch doesn't block your code.
- **Dropcontact** if your team works in spreadsheets and AI assistants, because one account and one pool of credits covers its REST API, MCP server, and Google Sheets add-on.
- **Snov.io** when you also want outreach from the same account, because its email finder sits inside a sales platform that also runs email campaigns.


Whichever you choose, run it on a sample of contacts whose addresses you already know before you buy credits in bulk. To try the Firecrawl Alexandria route,[create a free Firecrawl account](https://www.firecrawl.dev/app/alexandria) and ask your agent for a work email.
